subsystems.name: Quantum processing unit (QPU)
subsystems.role: the chip that performs the quantum computation.
parts: qubit chip (superconducting circuits, trapped ions, photonic circuits or neutral atoms)

subsystems.name: Physical environment
subsystems.role: maintains the extreme conditions each qubit modality needs to stay coherent.
parts: vacuum chamber and ion trap (trapped ions)

subsystems.name: Control and readout electronics
subsystems.role: generates the microwave, radio-frequency or optical pulses that manipulate qubits, and reads back their state.

subsystems.name: Classical orchestration layer
subsystems.role: translates user circuits into hardware instructions, schedules jobs and tracks device calibration.

subsystems.name: Cloud API and SDK
subsystems.role: the user-facing interface that lets remote users submit jobs without owning hardware.
parts: Python SDKs such as Qiskit, Cirq and the Braket SDK

subsystems.name: Networking and security
subsystems.role: moves circuits and results securely between user and provider.

subsystems.name: Hybrid runtime
subsystems.role: couples quantum hardware to classical high-performance computing for algorithms that alternate between the two.
parts: runtime environment for variational and iterative algorithms

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the processor
buildSteps.detail: Qubits are made in cleanroom processes: superconducting aluminium or niobium circuits on silicon, microfabricated ion traps, or photonic integrated circuits.

buildSteps.title: Package and cool the chip
buildSteps.detail: The chip is mounted, wire-bonded or coupled to signal lines, and installed in a dilution refrigerator or ultra-high-vacuum chamber with lasers, depending on the modality.

buildSteps.title: Bring up the control stack
buildSteps.detail: Room-temperature electronics are connected and calibrated so that digital commands produce the correct pulses at the qubit.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the qubits
buildSteps.detail: Engineers tune qubit frequencies, gate durations, pulse amplitudes and readout thresholds, then repeat this regularly because devices drift.

buildSteps.title: Build the orchestration service
buildSteps.detail: A compiler and transpiler map user circuits onto the physical qubit layout; a scheduler queues jobs and routes them to available devices.

buildSteps.title: Expose it through cloud APIs and SDKs
buildSteps.detail: The provider wraps access in a documented SDK, adds authentication, quotas, simulators and notebooks, and connects it to a cloud region.

buildSteps.title: Operate, monitor and price access
buildSteps.detail: The service tracks calibration, error rates and uptime, runs classical simulators for testing, and bills users per job, shot or time block.

prerequisites.why: cloud access needs real hardware on the other end, even if today's devices are small and noisy.
qubits only behave quantum-mechanically under carefully controlled conditions and signal chains.
queueing, authentication and remote job submission rely on mature data-centre and web-service technology.
without it, results from noisy hardware are hard to trust, so the software is as important as the chip.
reliable, large-scale quantum computation requires many physical qubits working together to correct errors.
porting a job between vendors is still difficult; common metrics would make cloud access more useful.

pathway.milestone: cloud access to noisy intermediate-scale quantum processors from several vendors, including IBM Quantum, Amazon Braket, Microsoft Azure Quantum and Rigetti
pathway.unlocks: researchers and students run small circuits remotely without owning a lab.

pathway.milestone: better error mitigation, larger qubit counts and tighter integration with classical high-performance computing
pathway.unlocks: practical hybrid algorithms and more credible benchmarking of quantum advantage.

pathway.milestone: early fault-tolerant quantum computers offered through cloud services
pathway.unlocks: niche problems in chemistry, materials and optimisation that classical machines cannot handle.

pathway.milestone: quantum processors embedded in mainstream cloud and supercomputing environments
pathway.unlocks: routine hybrid classical-quantum workflows and broad access to fault-tolerant machines.
